question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The toddler decided to make a mess because he wanted to ______ the attention of its parents.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. seek.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Seek" means to try to get or obtain something; to look for. The collocation "seek attention" is the fixed, natural expression in English for trying to draw notice to oneself. (ध्यान आकर्षित करने का प्रयास करना)

◦ Correct: The toddler decided to make a mess because he wanted to seek the attention of its parents.

• A child creating a mess deliberately is classic "attention-seeking" behaviour, so "seek" fits both the grammar and the meaning perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "elicit" means to draw out a response, reaction or information from someone (elicit a reply / elicit information). One elicits a reaction, not "attention" — the collocation is wrong.

• Option 3 "please" means to give satisfaction or pleasure to someone. "Please the attention" is meaningless; you please a person, not an abstract noun like attention.

• Option 4 "extract" means to pull or take out by force (extract a tooth / extract a confession). It carries a sense of force that does not suit "attention".

NOTE

• Common collocations with "attention": seek attention, pay attention, draw attention, attract attention, divert attention, bring to one's attention.

• Useful derivatives: seeker (noun — one who seeks), sought (past/past participle of seek). Remember the irregular form: seek – sought – sought.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Glimpse
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Glance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Glimpse" means a very brief, quick or partial look at something. Its closest synonym is "glance", which also means a quick, hurried look. (झलक / एक क्षणिक दृष्टि)

◦ Example: I caught a glimpse of the actor as his car sped past.

◦ Example: She threw a quick glance at her watch.

• Both words share the key idea of shortness of duration — the look lasts only a moment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Examine" means to inspect closely and in detail — the opposite of a hurried look.

• Option 3 "Stare" means to look fixedly for a long time, often rudely; it is a prolonged look, not a brief one.

• Option 4 "Observe" means to watch carefully and attentively, usually over a period of time, in order to notice something.

NOTE

• Synonyms of glimpse: glance, peek, peep, sighting, brief look. Antonyms: gaze, stare, gape, contemplate.

• Remember the family of "looking" words graded by duration: glimpse/glance (a second) → look (brief) → watch/observe (sustained) → stare/gaze (long and fixed) → scrutinise/examine (long and detailed).

question: Identify the sentence that contains correct spellings in the given context.
option_1: She acid the test despite being sleep-deprived from studying for nearly 24 hours straight.
option_2: She acad the test desspite being sleep-deprived from studying for nearly 24 hours straight.
option_3: She aced the test daspite being sleep-deprived from studying for nearly 24 hours strait.
option_4: She aced the test despite being sleep-deprived from studying for nearly 24 hours straight.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. She aced the test despite being sleep-deprived from studying for nearly 24 hours straight.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Three words decide this question, and only Option 4 spells all three correctly:

◦ "aced" — the verb "to ace (a test)" means to pass with flying colours / score very highly. (परीक्षा में शानदार प्रदर्शन करना)

◦ "despite" — a preposition meaning in spite of; notwithstanding. It is written as ONE word with a single "s": DE + SPITE.

◦ "straight" — meaning continuously, without a break ("24 hours straight").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly uses "acid" (an acid is a sour chemical substance) instead of "aced".

• Option 2 has two errors — "acad" (not a word) and "desspite" (double "s" is wrong).

• Option 3 has two errors — "daspite" (wrong vowel) and "strait" (a strait is a narrow channel of water, e.g., the Palk Strait; it does not mean "continuously").

NOTE

• Watch the classic homophone pair: straight (not bent / continuously) vs strait (a narrow sea passage; also "dire straits" = serious difficulty).

• "Despite" and "in spite of" are followed by a noun or gerund, never by a clause: despite being tired (✓), despite he was tired (✗).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The teacher assured: “You have completed your homework, __________?”
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. haven’t you.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a question tag. The rule is: a positive statement takes a negative tag, and the tag must repeat the same auxiliary verb and the same subject (as a pronoun) used in the statement.

◦ Statement: "You have completed your homework" — positive, auxiliary = have, subject = you.

◦ Therefore the tag must be the negative of "have" with "you": "haven't you?"

◦ Correct: You have completed your homework, haven't you?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "had you" and Option 2 "hadn't you" use the wrong auxiliary — the sentence uses the present perfect "have completed", not the past perfect "had completed".

• Option 4 "have you" is positive, but a positive statement requires a negative tag.

NOTE

• Question-tag rules for SSC:

◦ Positive statement → negative tag: She is coming, isn't she?

◦ Negative statement → positive tag: He didn't call, did he?

◦ Imperative → will you / won't you: Open the door, will you?

◦ "Let's ..." → shall we: Let's go, shall we?

◦ "I am ..." → aren't I: I am right, aren't I?

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

A _________________(distinct) sense of restlessness was bothering me when I left the cemetery.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. vague.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Distinct" means clear, definite, easily noticed and unmistakable. Its antonym is "vague", meaning unclear, indefinite, not sharply defined. (स्पष्ट का विलोम — अस्पष्ट / धुंधला)

◦ Correct: A vague sense of restlessness was bothering me when I left the cemetery.

• A "vague sense of restlessness" is also the natural collocation — an uneasy feeling one cannot pin down.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "terrible" (very bad, dreadful) is not the opposite of "distinct".

• Option 2 "critical" (crucial / fault-finding) is unrelated to clarity.

• Option 3 "prior" (earlier, previous) refers to time, not to clarity.

NOTE

• Synonyms of distinct: clear, definite, evident, marked, unmistakable, discernible. Antonyms: vague, indistinct, hazy, obscure, blurred.

• Do not confuse distinct (clear/separate) with distinctive (characteristic, serving to identify) — a distinct smell vs a distinctive uniform.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

With cloud streaming, people can play games from a / internet-connected device, avoiding the need for pricey / dedicated hardware such as a game console.
option_2: dedicated hardware such as a game console
option_3: With cloud streaming, people can play games from a
option_4: internet-connected device, avoiding the need for pricey
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. With cloud streaming, people can play games from a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is the article "a". The word that follows is "internet-connected device", which begins with the vowel sound /ɪ/. Before a vowel sound we must use "an", not "a".

◦ Correct: With cloud streaming, people can play games from an internet-connected device, avoiding the need for pricey dedicated hardware such as a game console.

• The choice between a and an depends on the SOUND that follows, not on the letter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Part "internet-connected device, avoiding the need for pricey" is correct — "pricey" (expensive) is a proper adjective and the participle phrase "avoiding ..." is correctly used.

• Part "dedicated hardware such as a game console" is correct — "hardware" is an uncountable noun and "such as" correctly introduces an example.

NOTE

• Article rules by sound:

◦ an before vowel sounds: an hour, an honest man, an MLA, an heir, an umbrella.

◦ a before consonant sounds even if the word starts with a vowel letter: a university, a European, a one-rupee coin, a useful book.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Keep someone at arm’s length
option_2: To avoid becoming too close or friendly with someone
option_4: Having energy again after being tired
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To avoid becoming too close or friendly with someone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "keep someone at arm's length" means to avoid becoming too friendly or intimate with someone; to maintain a deliberate distance. The image is of literally holding a person as far away as your arm can reach. (किसी से दूरी बनाए रखना)

◦ Example: Ever since the quarrel, she has kept her cousin at arm's length.

◦ Example: Wise investors keep dubious schemes at arm's length.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to ruin someone's plans" is the meaning of idioms like "upset the applecart" or "put a spanner in the works".

• Option 3 "angry about something" corresponds to "hot under the collar" or "see red".

• Option 4 "having energy again after being tired" corresponds to "get a second wind" or "recharge one's batteries".

NOTE

• Related expressions: an "arm's-length transaction" in business/law means a deal between parties who are independent of each other, with no special relationship.

• Similar distance idioms: "give someone a wide berth" (avoid someone), "steer clear of" (stay away from).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) This fridge / (B) comes including / (C) a 5-year / (D) warranty.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. B.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part (B) "comes including" is wrong. When a product is sold together with something, the correct expression is "comes with". "Including" is a preposition used to show that something is part of a larger group ("the bill, including taxes"), and it cannot follow "comes" in this sense.

◦ Correct: This fridge comes with a 5-year warranty.

• "Come with" is the standard collocation for accompanying features/accessories: The phone comes with a charger.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Part (A) "This fridge" is correct — a singular demonstrative + singular noun.

• Part (C) "a 5-year" is correct — when a number + noun works as a compound adjective before a noun, the noun stays singular and hyphenated: a 5-year warranty, a 10-rupee note, a three-hour meeting.

• Part (D) "warranty" is correctly spelt and correctly used.

NOTE

• Useful phrasal patterns: come with (be supplied along with), come across (find by chance), come by (obtain), come up with (produce an idea), come round (regain consciousness / change one's opinion).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

One who looks at the dark side of life
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Pessimist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "pessimist" is a person who always looks at the dark/gloomy side of things and expects the worst to happen. (निराशावादी)

◦ Example: A pessimist sees difficulty in every opportunity; an optimist sees opportunity in every difficulty.

• The word comes from the Latin pessimus meaning "worst".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Physicist" — a person who specialises in physics (unrelated).

• Option 2 "Optimist" — a person who looks at the bright side of life and hopes for the best; this is the exact opposite of the required word.

• Option 4 "Idealist" — a person guided by ideals rather than practical considerations.

NOTE

• Frequently asked one-word substitutes of this family: Optimist (hopeful person), Pessimist (gloomy person), Realist (one who accepts things as they are), Cynic (one who distrusts others' motives), Misanthrope (one who hates mankind), Philanthropist (one who loves and helps mankind), Egotist (one who talks constantly about himself).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Many a things are used for the show.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. a thing is.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "many a" is always followed by a singular noun and a singular verb, even though its meaning is plural.

◦ Structure: Many a + singular noun + singular verb.

◦ Correct: Many a thing is used for the show.

• Hence "a things are" must become "a thing is" — the noun changes to singular ("thing") and the verb to singular ("is").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a things is" keeps the plural noun "things" with a singular verb — mismatched.

• Option 2 "a things were" keeps both the plural noun and a plural verb — wrong after "many a".

• Option 4 "a thing were" has the right singular noun but the plural/past-subjunctive verb "were"; the sentence is in the present tense, so "is" is required.

NOTE

• Compare the two structures:

◦ Many a student has passed the exam. (singular)

◦ Many students have passed the exam. (plural)

• Similar singular-taking expressions: each, every, either, neither, more than one, one of the + plural noun (the verb agrees with "one").

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’.

This film is a non-stop riot that many cite as one of the funny films of all time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. funniest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "one of the ..." is always followed by a superlative degree + plural noun. So "one of the funny films" must become "one of the funniest films".

◦ Structure: one of the + superlative + plural noun.

◦ Correct: This film is a non-stop riot that many cite as one of the funniest films of all time.

• "Funny" is a two-syllable adjective ending in "-y", so it forms its degrees by changing "y" to "i" and adding "-er/-est": funny – funnier – funniest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "no rectification needed" is wrong because the positive degree "funny" cannot follow "one of the".

• Option 3 "more funny" is doubly wrong — the comparative of "funny" is "funnier" (not "more funny"), and a comparative cannot follow "one of the" anyway.

• Option 4 "funnier" is the comparative degree; the structure demands the superlative.

NOTE

• Similar patterns: one of the best players, one of the most beautiful cities, one of the tallest buildings.

• Note also the subject–verb rule: "One of the funniest films is ..." — the verb agrees with "one" (singular).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Transmisible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Transmisible" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "transmissible", meaning capable of being transmitted or passed on (especially a disease). (संचरणीय / फैलने योग्य)

◦ Spelling key: TRANS + MISS + IBLE — note the double "s" (from "transmiss-") and the ending "-ible".

◦ Example: Tuberculosis is a highly transmissible disease.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Essence" (the intrinsic nature or indispensable quality of something) is correctly spelt.

• "Aggregate" (a total formed by combining several separate items) is correctly spelt.

• "Assembly" (a group of people gathered together; a legislative body) is correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Word family: transmit – transmitted – transmission – transmissible – transmitter. The double "s" carries through from "transmission".

• Related confusables ending in "-ible": permissible, admissible, accessible, responsible, feasible. Those in "-able": manageable, comfortable, dependable, reliable.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who regards the whole world as his country
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Cosmopolitan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "cosmopolitan" is a person who regards the whole world as his country / who is free from national prejudices and is at home everywhere. (विश्वनागरिक)

◦ The word comes from Greek kosmos (world) + polites (citizen) — literally a "citizen of the world".

◦ Example: Widely travelled and multilingual, he was a true cosmopolitan.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Pacifist" — one who is opposed to war and believes in peace.

• Option 3 "Contemporary" — one who lives at the same time as another; belonging to the present time.

• Option 4 "Celibate" — one who abstains from marriage and sexual relations.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: Patriot (one who loves his country), Chauvinist (one with exaggerated, aggressive patriotism), Xenophobe (one who fears/hates foreigners), Emigrant (one who leaves his country to settle elsewhere), Immigrant (one who comes into a foreign country to settle).

• "Cosmopolitan" is also used as an adjective for a city with people from many countries — Mumbai is a cosmopolitan city.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

The team played / really well, but / they lose the game / in the final minutes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. they lose the game.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes a past event — "The team played ... in the final minutes". The verb in the third segment must therefore also be in the past tense: "lost", not the present-tense "lose". This is the rule of tense consistency (sequence of tenses) in a compound sentence joined by "but".

◦ Correct: The team played really well, but they lost the game in the final minutes.

• The past tense of "lose" is "lost" (lose – lost – lost).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "The team played" is correct — "team" is a collective noun taking a singular verb here, and "played" is the correct past form.

• "really well, but" is correct — the adverb "really" correctly modifies the adverb "well" (not "good", which is an adjective).

• "in the final minutes" is a correct prepositional phrase of time.

NOTE

• Do not confuse lose (verb — to be deprived of; rhymes with "choose") with loose (adjective — not tight) and loss (noun).

• When two clauses are joined by a coordinating conjunction (and, but, or, so), they should normally be in the same tense unless the meaning demands otherwise.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

The school shall reopened / after summer / vacations of / one month.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The school shall reopened.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A modal auxiliary ("shall, will, can, may, must, should, would, could, might") is always followed by the base form (V1) of the verb — never by the past form (V2) or past participle (V3).

◦ Wrong: The school shall reopened ...

◦ Correct: The school shall reopen after summer vacations of one month.

• "Reopened" is the past form; after "shall" it must become the bare infinitive "reopen".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "after summer" is a correct prepositional phrase.

• "vacations of" and "one month" are acceptable as printed in the given context.

NOTE

• Modal + V1 examples: He can swim, She must go, They will come, You should study.

• For the passive after a modal use modal + be + V3: The school shall be reopened by the government.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

They waited with anxiety for the final results.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Calmness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Anxiety" means a feeling of worry, nervousness or unease about an uncertain outcome. Its antonym is "calmness", meaning a state of peace, composure and freedom from agitation. (चिंता / बेचैनी का विलोम — शांति)

◦ Example: They waited with anxiety (worry) — the opposite would be waiting with calmness (composure).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Shrewdness" means sharp practical judgement, cleverness — unrelated to worry.

• Option 2 "Wilderness" means an uncultivated, uninhabited region — a place, not a feeling.

• Option 3 "Feebleness" means weakness, lack of strength — not the opposite of anxiety.

NOTE

• Synonyms of anxiety: worry, apprehension, unease, disquiet, angst, foreboding. Antonyms: calmness, composure, serenity, tranquillity, equanimity.

• Distinguish anxiety (a state of worry) from anxiousness and from eagerness — "anxious to help" can mean "keen to help".

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Jack took on three jobs at once but soon realised he had _____________.
option_2: taken it with a grain of salt
option_3: bitten off more than he could chew
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. bitten off more than he could chew.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "bite off more than one can chew" means to take on more work or responsibility than one can handle. Jack accepted three jobs at once — clearly more than he could manage. (क्षमता से अधिक काम अपने ऊपर ले लेना)

◦ Correct: Jack took on three jobs at once but soon realised he had bitten off more than he could chew.

• Note the correct participle form "bitten" after "had" (bite – bit – bitten).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "cut corners" means to do something in the cheapest or easiest way, sacrificing quality.

• Option 2 "take it with a grain (pinch) of salt" means to regard something with scepticism, not to believe it fully.

• Option 4 "play it by ear" means to improvise / act without a fixed plan as the situation develops.

NOTE

• Similar idioms about overload: "have too much on one's plate", "spread oneself too thin", "burn the candle at both ends".

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

The CEO has _____________ than worrying about individual customer complaints.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. bigger fish to fry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "have bigger (other) fish to fry" means to have more important matters to attend to. A CEO has larger, strategic concerns than individual customer complaints. (अधिक महत्वपूर्ण काम होना)

◦ Correct: The CEO has bigger fish to fry than worrying about individual customer complaints.

• The comparative word "than" in the sentence is the structural clue — only "bigger fish to fry" contains a comparative and fits with "than".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "take a rain check" means to politely decline an invitation now but accept it at a later date.

• Option 3 "throw caution to the wind(s)" means to behave recklessly, taking a big risk.

• Option 4 "walk/skate on thin ice" means to be in a risky or precarious situation.

NOTE

• Related idioms of priority: "first things first", "put something on the back burner" (postpone), "a bigger picture" (the wider view).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Vaccum.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vaccum" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "vacuum", meaning a space entirely devoid of matter; emptiness. (निर्वात / शून्य)

◦ Spelling key: VAC + U + UM — one "c" and double "u". Learners commonly reverse this and write double "c" with one "u".

◦ Example: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Perceive" (to become aware of through the senses) is correctly spelt — remember the rule "i before e except after c": receive, deceive, conceive, perceive.

• "Recognition" (the act of recognising) is correctly spelt.

• "Shield" (a protective covering) is correctly spelt — here "i before e" applies normally.

NOTE

• Word family: vacuum, vacuous (empty-headed), vacuity, vacant, vacate, vacation — all from Latin vacuus meaning "empty".

• "Vacuum" is one of very few English words with a double "u"; others include "continuum" and "residuum".

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

I know it was wrong to distract his friends, but ________.
option_1: all’s fair in love and war
option_3: all’s unfair in love and war
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. all’s fair in love and war.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The proverb "All's fair in love and war" means in certain intense situations (such as love or conflict) any method, even an unfair one, may be considered acceptable. It is used to justify slightly unscrupulous behaviour, exactly as the speaker does here. (प्रेम और युद्ध में सब जायज़ है)

◦ Correct: I know it was wrong to distract his friends, but all's fair in love and war.

• The saying is attributed to John Lyly's Euphues (1578).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 — "all's unfair in the world", "all's unfair in love and war" and "all's fair in the world" — are distorted, non-existent forms of the proverb. Idioms and proverbs are fixed expressions: not a single word may be altered.

NOTE

• Other fixed proverbs commonly tested: "A stitch in time saves nine", "Barking dogs seldom bite", "Every cloud has a silver lining", "Make hay while the sun shines".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

(1)___ the breakfast table the next morning, there was no sign of my wife. I (2)___ she was sleeping late, but Gladolia, upon being questioned, only (3)___ her head, (4)___ something, and turned the whites of her eyes up to the ceiling. I was glad when the meal was (5)___ and hurried to the library for another try at that story.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. At.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "at" is used with the table when we speak of people seated for a meal: "at the breakfast table", "at the dinner table", "at table".

◦ Correct: At the breakfast table the next morning, there was no sign of my wife.

• "At" indicates a point/position where an activity takes place, which is exactly the sense here — the place where the family gathers to eat.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "On" the table would mean placed upon its surface (like a plate or a book), not seated around it.

• Option 2 "Above" means vertically higher than, with no contact — meaningless here.

• Option 3 "Upon" is a more formal variant of "on" and carries the same wrong meaning of resting on the surface.

NOTE

• Fixed prepositional phrases with "at": at the table, at school, at home, at work, at the door, at the top, at noon, at night.

• Compare: The food is on the table (surface) but The family is at the table (seated for a meal).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

(1)___ the breakfast table the next morning, there was no sign of my wife. I (2)___ she was sleeping late, but Gladolia, upon being questioned, only (3)___ her head, (4)___ something, and turned the whites of her eyes up to the ceiling. I was glad when the meal was (5)___ and hurried to the library for another try at that story.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. concluded.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Concluded" means arrived at a judgement or opinion by reasoning from the available evidence. The narrator does not see his wife at breakfast and therefore infers that she is sleeping late — an inference, not a decision.

◦ Correct: I concluded she was sleeping late, but Gladolia ... only shook her head.

• The verb "conclude" naturally takes a that-clause: I concluded (that) she was sleeping late.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "accepted" means to receive or agree to something already offered; one does not "accept" a fact one has just guessed.

• Option 2 "decided" refers to making a choice about one's own action; the wife's sleeping is not the narrator's choice to make.

• Option 3 "examined" means to inspect closely — it cannot take a that-clause in this way and does not fit the meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of conclude (in this sense): infer, deduce, gather, surmise, reckon, judge.

• "Conclude" also means "to bring to an end" — He concluded his speech with a quotation.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

(1)___ the breakfast table the next morning, there was no sign of my wife. I (2)___ she was sleeping late, but Gladolia, upon being questioned, only (3)___ her head, (4)___ something, and turned the whites of her eyes up to the ceiling. I was glad when the meal was (5)___ and hurried to the library for another try at that story.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. shook.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed collocation is "to shake one's head", meaning to move the head from side to side to express refusal, denial, doubt or disapproval. Gladolia, when questioned, only shook her head — she would not or could not say anything. (सिर हिलाना — इनकार में)

◦ Correct: ... but Gladolia, upon being questioned, only shook her head, muttered something ...

• The past tense of "shake" is "shook" (shake – shook – shaken), which matches the past-tense narration.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "adjusted" (altered slightly to fit) does not collocate with "head" in this sense.

• Option 2 "rotated" (turned in a circle about an axis) is technical and unnatural for a human gesture.

• Option 4 "stirred" (mixed with a spoon / moved slightly) does not go with "head".

NOTE

• Gesture collocations: shake one's head (to say no), nod one's head (to say yes), shrug one's shoulders (to show indifference), raise an eyebrow (to show surprise).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

(1)___ the breakfast table the next morning, there was no sign of my wife. I (2)___ she was sleeping late, but Gladolia, upon being questioned, only (3)___ her head, (4)___ something, and turned the whites of her eyes up to the ceiling. I was glad when the meal was (5)___ and hurried to the library for another try at that story.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. muttered.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Muttered" means spoke in a low, indistinct voice, often unwillingly or in complaint. This fits perfectly with a servant who refuses to answer clearly, only shaking her head and rolling her eyes. (बुदबुदाना)

◦ Correct: ... only shook her head, muttered something, and turned the whites of her eyes up to the ceiling.

• "Mutter something" is a natural collocation — the words are unclear, so the object is vague.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mugged" means attacked and robbed in a public place (or, in Indian usage, learnt by rote) — quite unrelated.

• Option 2 "muffed" means bungled or handled clumsily (muffed a catch) — it does not describe speech.

• Option 3 "mutilated" means severely damaged or disfigured by cutting off a part — far too violent and irrelevant.

NOTE

• Manner-of-speaking verbs often tested: mutter/mumble (speak unclearly), murmur (speak softly), whisper (speak breathily), grumble (complain), stammer/stutter (speak with hesitations), exclaim (cry out suddenly).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

(1)___ the breakfast table the next morning, there was no sign of my wife. I (2)___ she was sleeping late, but Gladolia, upon being questioned, only (3)___ her head, (4)___ something, and turned the whites of her eyes up to the ceiling. I was glad when the meal was (5)___ and hurried to the library for another try at that story.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. over.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Be over" means to be finished / at an end. "The meal was over" is the standard expression for a meal having come to an end, after which the narrator hurried to the library.

◦ Correct: I was glad when the meal was over and hurried to the library for another try at that story.

• Here "over" functions as a predicative adjective/adverb after the verb "be", which is exactly the slot the blank occupies.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "removed" would mean the meal was physically taken away — it changes the meaning and is unidiomatic here.

• Option 3 "through" would need a subject that is a person: I was through with the meal (✓), but the meal was through (✗).

• Option 4 "undone" means not done / unfastened / ruined — the opposite of finished.

NOTE

• Expressions with "over" meaning "finished": The match is over, It's all over, The worst is over, Game over.

• Contrast "over" (finished) with "over with" (Let's get it over with = finish an unpleasant task).

question: According to Census of India 2011, what was the total population of India (approx)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 121 Crore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, the total population of India was about 121 crore (1,210 million / 1.21 billion) — precisely 1,210,854,977. (भारत की जनसंख्या 2011 — लगभग 121 करोड़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India and the 7th after Independence. Its slogan was "Our Census, Our Future".

• Density of population: 382 persons per sq. km. Sex ratio: 943 females per 1000 males. Literacy rate: 74.04%.

• Most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim. Most populous UT — Delhi.

• Highest literacy — Kerala (93.91%); lowest — Bihar (61.8%). Highest sex ratio — Kerala (1084); lowest — Haryana (879).

NOTE

• The Census in India is conducted every 10 years under the Census Act, 1948, by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, Ministry of Home Affairs.

• The first census in India was held in 1872 under Lord Mayo; the first complete, synchronous census was in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

question: Chhau is a major dance tradition of India. In which of the following Indian states is the dance form NOT prevalent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhau is a semi-classical, martial folk dance tradition practised in three eastern states — Odisha, West Bengal and Jharkhand. It is NOT prevalent in Madhya Pradesh. (छऊ नृत्य — ओडिशा, पश्चिम बंगाल, झारखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The three recognised styles of Chhau are:

◦ Seraikela Chhau — Jharkhand (dancers wear masks).

◦ Purulia Chhau — West Bengal (large, elaborate masks).

◦ Mayurbhanj Chhau — Odisha (performed without masks).

• Chhau blends martial arts (Pharikhanda), acrobatics and athletics with themes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas.

• It was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

NOTE

• Folk dances of Madhya Pradesh include Gaur, Matki, Grida, Phulpati, Karma and Jawara — not Chhau.

• India's eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: In November 2022, which state became the first North-East state to approve Mental Health and Social Care Policy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2022, Meghalaya became the first North-Eastern state (and one of the first in India) to approve a dedicated "Mental Health and Social Care Policy". (मेघालय — मानसिक स्वास्थ्य नीति)

• The policy aims to make mental-health care accessible, affordable and stigma-free, integrating counselling and social care into primary health services.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Meghalaya ("the abode of clouds") became a full state on 21 January 1972; capital — Shillong. Major tribes: Khasi, Jaintia and Garo.

• At the national level, mental health is governed by the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, which decriminalised attempted suicide and guaranteed the right to access mental healthcare.

• The National Tele Mental Health Programme (Tele-MANAS) was launched in October 2022.

NOTE

• The National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) has been running since 1982; the District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) was added in 1996.

• World Mental Health Day is observed on 10 October every year.

question: In which state is Vishakhapatnam Port located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Visakhapatnam Port is located in the state of Andhra Pradesh, on the east coast of India along the Bay of Bengal. (विशाखापत्तनम बंदरगाह — आंध्र प्रदेश)

• It is one of India's major ports and is famous as the deepest landlocked port in the country, handling large volumes of iron ore, coal and petroleum.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Visakhapatnam is also the headquarters of the Eastern Naval Command of the Indian Navy and hosts Hindustan Shipyard.

• Major ports on the east coast: Kolkata (Syama Prasad Mookerjee), Paradip (Odisha), Visakhapatnam (AP), Chennai, Kamarajar/Ennore (TN), V. O. Chidambaranar/Tuticorin (TN).

• Major ports on the west coast: Kandla (Deendayal, Gujarat), Mumbai, Jawaharlal Nehru (Nhava Sheva), Mormugao (Goa), New Mangalore (Karnataka), Cochin (Kerala).

NOTE

• India has 13 major ports (12 government-administered plus Port Blair). Major ports come under the Union Government (Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways); minor ports are under state governments.

question: Who among the following is the Indian classical dancer who masters both Bharatanatyam and Odissi dancing style?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sonal Mansingh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sonal Mansingh is the celebrated Indian classical dancer who has mastered both Bharatanatyam and Odissi. (सोनल मानसिंह — भरतनाट्यम एवं ओडिसी)

• She was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2003) — becoming the first woman dancer to receive it — and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. She was later nominated to the Rajya Sabha (2018).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shovana Narayan — a renowned exponent of Kathak (and a former Indian Audit and Accounts Service officer).

• Guru Bipin Singh — the great guru of Manipuri dance.

• Padma Subrahmanyam — a leading exponent of Bharatanatyam and the creator of "Bharata Nrityam".

• Sonal Mansingh founded the Centre for Indian Classical Dances (CICD), New Delhi, in 1977.

NOTE

• Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha, characterised by the tribhanga posture and sculpturesque poses derived from temple carvings; Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra.

question: Which bacteria was discovered by Barry Marshall and Robin Warren that colonises the human stomach and causes chronic superficial gastritis ulcers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Helicobacter pylori.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is the spiral-shaped bacterium discovered by the Australian scientists Barry Marshall and Robin Warren. It colonises the human stomach lining and causes chronic superficial gastritis, peptic ulcers and, in some cases, stomach cancer. (हेलिकोबैक्टर पाइलोरी)

• For this discovery the two were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2005.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Campylobacter jejuni — a common cause of food poisoning / bacterial diarrhoea.

• Neisseria gonorrhoeae — the bacterium that causes the sexually transmitted disease gonorrhoea.

• Entamoeba histolytica — not a bacterium at all but a protozoan parasite, which causes amoebic dysentery.

• H. pylori survives the stomach's acid by producing the enzyme urease, which neutralises acid around it.

NOTE

• Before this discovery, ulcers were blamed on stress and spicy food; today they are treated with antibiotics plus proton-pump inhibitors. Barry Marshall famously drank a culture of the bacteria himself to prove the link.

question: Which of the following states witnesses the first onset of the monsoon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kerala witnesses the first onset of the South-West Monsoon in India, normally around 1 June every year. The moisture-laden winds of the Arabian Sea branch strike the Western Ghats first and give Kerala its first heavy showers. (केरल — मानसून का प्रथम आगमन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The South-West Monsoon advances from Kerala northwards, covering the whole country by about 15 July, and begins to withdraw from north-west India around mid-September.

• The monsoon has two branches — the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch. Mawsynram and Cherrapunji (Meghalaya) receive the highest rainfall in the world.

• Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh are reached last, in late June–early July, and receive comparatively less monsoon rain.

NOTE

• The India Meteorological Department (IMD), established in 1875 with headquarters at New Delhi, officially declares the onset of the monsoon over Kerala.

• The North-East (retreating) Monsoon brings winter rainfall mainly to Tamil Nadu and the Coromandel Coast in October–December.

question: What is a prominent trend in the microfinance sector in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Integration of mobile banking services.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A prominent, well-documented trend in India's microfinance sector is the integration of mobile banking and digital financial services. Microfinance institutions (MFIs) now use mobile apps, UPI, Aadhaar-enabled payments and e-KYC to disburse loans, collect repayments and reach remote borrowers cheaply. (माइक्रोफाइनेंस में मोबाइल बैंकिंग का एकीकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options describe the opposite of current trends: the sector is moving towards faster, technology-driven approvals, greater (not decreased) reliance on digital technology, and a strong focus on women borrowers — women form the overwhelming majority of microfinance clients through Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups.

• Microfinance provides small-value loans, savings and insurance to low-income households that lack access to formal banking.

• NABARD launched the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme in 1992, the world's largest microfinance programme.

NOTE

• The Reserve Bank of India regulates NBFC-MFIs; its revised Regulatory Framework for Microfinance Loans (2022) defines a microfinance loan as a collateral-free loan to a household with annual income up to ₹3 lakh.

• Bandhan Bank began as a microfinance institution before becoming a universal bank; Muhammad Yunus of Bangladesh (Grameen Bank) is called the "father of microfinance" and won the Nobel Peace Prize (2006).

question: Ustad Bismillah Khan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shehnai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916–2006) was the legendary Indian musician associated with the "Shehnai", a double-reed wind (aerophone) instrument traditionally played at weddings and temple ceremonies. He almost single-handedly raised the shehnai to the concert stage. (उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खान — शहनाई)

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, India's highest civilian honour, and also the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He famously played the shehnai from the Red Fort on 15 August 1947, on India's first Independence Day, at the invitation of Pandit Nehru.

• Other instruments and their masters:

◦ Sarod — Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, Ustad Ali Akbar Khan.

◦ Sitar — Pandit Ravi Shankar, Ustad Vilayat Khan.

◦ Sarangi — Pandit Ram Narayan.

NOTE

• Classification of Indian instruments: Tata Vadya (string — sitar, sarod, veena), Sushira Vadya (wind — shehnai, flute, nadaswaram), Avanaddha Vadya (percussion with membrane — tabla, mridangam), Ghana Vadya (solid/idiophone — manjira, jaltarang).

question: The famous coal mining region ‘Korba’ is located in which state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Korba, one of India's most important coal mining regions, is located in the state of Chhattisgarh. It lies in the Hasdeo river valley and is famous for both its coalfields and its huge thermal power plants. (कोरबा — छत्तीसगढ़)

• Korba is often called the "Power Capital of India" because of the large NTPC and CSEB thermal power stations there.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's coal reserves lie mainly in the Gondwana rock formations of eastern and central India — Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana.

• Other famous coalfields: Jharia, Bokaro, Giridih (Jharkhand); Raniganj (West Bengal); Talcher (Odisha); Singrauli (MP); Singareni (Telangana).

• Jharkhand and Odisha are the largest coal-producing states of India.

NOTE

• Types of coal in decreasing order of carbon content and quality: Anthracite (best) > Bituminous > Lignite > Peat (poorest). Most Indian coal is bituminous; lignite is found mainly at Neyveli (Tamil Nadu).

• Coal India Limited (CIL), established in 1975, is the world's largest coal-producing company.

question: What do you mean by balanced budget?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Expenditure equal to revenue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "balanced budget" is one in which the government's total estimated expenditure is exactly equal to its total estimated revenue/receipts for a financial year. (संतुलित बजट — व्यय = आय)

◦ Balanced budget: Total Expenditure = Total Revenue.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Surplus budget — revenue exceeds expenditure (Revenue > Expenditure). It is used to control inflation by withdrawing money from circulation.

• Deficit budget — expenditure exceeds revenue (Expenditure > Revenue). Recommended by J. M. Keynes during a depression, as it boosts demand and employment; India generally presents a deficit budget.

• Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − Total receipts (excluding borrowings). Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts. Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit − Interest payments.

NOTE

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution as the "Annual Financial Statement". Since 2017 it is presented on 1 February, and the Railway Budget was merged with it in the same year.

• The FRBM Act, 2003 (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management) sets targets for reducing fiscal and revenue deficits.

question: Rajgir Mahotsav is a beautiful representation of history, religion, art and culture. It is a three-day celebration in ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Rajgir Mahotsav" is a three-day cultural festival celebrated at Rajgir in the Nalanda district of Bihar. It showcases the region's history, religion, art and culture through folk dances, classical music, opera and handicrafts. (राजगीर महोत्सव — बिहार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rajgir (ancient Rajagriha) was the first capital of the Magadha empire under the Haryanka dynasty (Bimbisara and Ajatashatru) before the capital shifted to Pataliputra.

• The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajgir (Saptaparni caves) in 483 BCE under the patronage of Ajatashatru. Rajgir is also sacred to Jainism — Lord Mahavira spent many rainy seasons here.

• Rajgir is famous for its hot springs (Brahmakund), the Vishwa Shanti Stupa (Peace Pagoda), Griddhakuta hill and India's first Ropeway. Nearby lies the ancient Nalanda University (a UNESCO World Heritage Site).

NOTE

• Other festivals of Bihar: Chhath Puja, Sonepur Mela (Asia's largest cattle fair), Pitrapaksha Mela (Gaya), Bihula-Bishahari and Sama-Chakeva.

question: The famous novel ‘The God Of Small Things’ is written by ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arundhati Roy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The God of Small Things" (1997) is the celebrated debut novel of the Indian author Arundhati Roy. It won the Booker Prize in 1997, making her the first Indian woman to win the award. (अरुंधति रॉय)

• The novel is set in Ayemenem, Kerala, and tells the story of the fraternal twins Rahel and Estha, exploring caste, family and forbidden love.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Her second novel is "The Ministry of Utmost Happiness" (2017). Her non-fiction includes "The End of Imagination", "Walking with the Comrades" and "Listening to Grasshoppers".

• Shashi Tharoor — The Great Indian Novel, An Era of Darkness, Why I Am a Hindu.

• Ruskin Bond — The Room on the Roof, The Blue Umbrella, A Flight of Pigeons.

• Vikram Seth — A Suitable Boy, The Golden Gate, An Equal Music.

NOTE

• Indian-origin Booker Prize winners: V. S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981 – Midnight's Children), Arundhati Roy (1997), Kiran Desai (2006 – The Inheritance of Loss), Aravind Adiga (2008 – The White Tiger). Geetanjali Shree won the International Booker Prize (2022) for Tomb of Sand (Ret Samadhi).

question: The Men's Junior Hockey Asia Cup 2023, which was won by India, was held at _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Oman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Men's Junior Hockey Asia Cup 2023 was held at Salalah, Oman, and was won by India, who defeated Pakistan 2–1 in the final. (जूनियर हॉकी एशिया कप 2023 — ओमान)

• This was India's fourth Junior Asia Cup title (after 2004, 2008 and 2015).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The tournament is organised by the Asian Hockey Federation (AHF) and acts as a qualifier for the Junior Hockey World Cup.

• India's captain in the 2023 edition was Uttam Singh, who was also adjudged the Player of the Tournament.

• Hockey India is the governing body for hockey in India; the international federation is the FIH (Fédération Internationale de Hockey), founded in 1924.

NOTE

• India's men's hockey team has won 8 Olympic gold medals (1928–1980) and the 1975 World Cup. At the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, India won a bronze medal after 41 years.

• Major Dhyan Chand, the "Wizard of Hockey", is honoured with National Sports Day on 29 August, his birth anniversary.

question: In the context of the Revolt of 1857, Mangal Pandey belonged to which Bengal native Infantry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 34.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mangal Pandey was a sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry, stationed at Barrackpore (near Kolkata). On 29 March 1857 he attacked his British officers, and he was hanged on 8 April 1857 — an act widely regarded as the spark of the Revolt of 1857. (मंगल पांडे — 34वीं बंगाल नेटिव इन्फैंट्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The immediate cause of the revolt was the introduction of the Enfield rifle, whose greased cartridges (rumoured to contain cow and pig fat) had to be bitten open, offending both Hindu and Muslim sepoys.

• The revolt formally broke out at Meerut on 10 May 1857, and the rebels marched to Delhi and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar as Emperor of India.

• Centres and leaders: Delhi – Bakht Khan; Kanpur – Nana Sahib & Tantia Tope; Lucknow – Begum Hazrat Mahal; Jhansi – Rani Lakshmibai; Bihar (Jagdishpur) – Kunwar Singh; Bareilly – Khan Bahadur Khan; Faizabad – Maulvi Ahmadullah.

NOTE

• After the revolt, the Government of India Act, 1858 ended East India Company rule and transferred power to the British Crown; Lord Canning became the first Viceroy of India.

• V. D. Savarkar called the revolt "The First War of Indian Independence".

question: Which of the following countries did India beat in the final to win the 2021 SAFF Championship?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nepal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won the 2021 SAFF Championship (held in Malé, Maldives, in October 2021) by beating Nepal 3–0 in the final. (सैफ चैंपियनशिप 2021 — भारत ने नेपाल को हराया)

• Sunil Chhetri scored twice and Suresh Singh Wangjam once in the final; Chhetri was the tournament's leading Indian scorer.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This was India's 8th SAFF Championship title. India later won the 2023 SAFF Championship as well, beating Kuwait on penalties in Bengaluru — making it India's 9th title.

• The SAFF (South Asian Football Federation) Championship began in 1993 and involves India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Maldives and Bhutan.

• Sunil Chhetri is India's all-time leading goal-scorer and one of the highest international scorers among active players.

NOTE

• The All India Football Federation (AIFF) was founded in 1937; India's national football team is nicknamed the "Blue Tigers".

• India's best performance in the Asian Games football was gold in 1951 and 1962.

question: Vinesh Phogat became the first Indian woman wrestler to win how many medals at World Championships?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vinesh Phogat became the first Indian woman wrestler to win two medals at the World Wrestling Championships — a bronze in 2019 (Nur-Sultan, Kazakhstan) and another bronze in 2022 (Belgrade, Serbia). (विनेश फोगाट — विश्व चैंपियनशिप में दो पदक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Vinesh Phogat is also the first Indian woman wrestler to win gold at both the Asian Games (2018, Jakarta) and the Commonwealth Games (2014, 2018, 2022).

• She was awarded the Arjuna Award (2016) and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna / Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (2020).

• She belongs to the famous Phogat wrestling family of Haryana; her cousins Geeta and Babita Phogat inspired the film Dangal.

NOTE

• Indian wrestlers who have won Olympic medals: K. D. Jadhav (1952 bronze), Sushil Kumar (2008 bronze, 2012 silver), Yogeshwar Dutt (2012 bronze), Sakshi Malik (2016 bronze), Ravi Dahiya (2020 silver), Bajrang Punia (2020 bronze).

• Sakshi Malik was the first Indian woman wrestler to win an Olympic medal (Rio 2016).

question: What is the purpose of the Cultural and Educational Rights?
option_2: To protect the language, culture, and religion of the minority communities
solution_text:
The correct answer is To protect the language, culture, and religion of the minority communities.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29 and 30) are intended to protect the language, script, culture and religion of minority communities and to enable them to preserve their distinct identity. (सांस्कृतिक एवं शैक्षिक अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 29-30)

◦ Article 29 — Protection of the interests of minorities: any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture has the right to conserve it; no citizen shall be denied admission to a State-aided institution on grounds of religion, race, caste or language.

◦ Article 30 — Right of all minorities (religious or linguistic) to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The six Fundamental Rights in Part III of the Constitution are:

◦ Right to Equality (Articles 14–18)

◦ Right to Freedom (Articles 19–22)

◦ Right against Exploitation (Articles 23–24)

◦ Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25–28)

◦ Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29–30)

◦ Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32)

• "To prevent exploitation" is the purpose of Articles 23–24 (prohibition of human trafficking, forced labour and child labour), not of Articles 29–30.

NOTE

• The Right to Property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment (1978) and made a legal right under Article 300A.

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the "heart and soul of the Constitution".

question: In optics, which term refers to the opening of the diaphragm of a lens that spatially limits the propagation of light?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aperture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In optics, the "aperture" is the opening of the diaphragm of a lens through which light passes; it spatially limits the propagation of light and thus controls how much light reaches the image/sensor. (द्वारक / एपर्चर)

• The aperture size is expressed as an f-number (f/stop), e.g., f/2.8, f/8. A smaller f-number = a wider aperture = more light and a shallower depth of field.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Collimator — an optical device that narrows a beam of light so that the rays become parallel; used in spectrometers and telescopes.

• Apostilb — an old unit of luminance (brightness).

• Meniscus — a lens that is convex on one side and concave on the other (also the curved upper surface of a liquid in a tube).

NOTE

• In photography the "exposure triangle" is aperture + shutter speed + ISO.

• Other optics terms for SSC: focal length (distance from the lens to its focus), power of a lens = 1/focal length in metres (unit dioptre), magnification, and the lens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f.

question: Lata Mangeshkar was awarded by the India's highest civilian honour ‘Bharat Ratna’ in the year _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2001.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary playback singer Lata Mangeshkar was conferred the "Bharat Ratna", India's highest civilian honour, in the year 2001. (लता मंगेशकर — भारत रत्न, 2001)

• She was only the second singer/musician to receive it, after M. S. Subbulakshmi (1998).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Lata Mangeshkar (1929–2022), called the "Nightingale of India" (स्वर कोकिला), recorded songs in over 36 languages. Her other honours include the Padma Bhushan (1969), Padma Vibhushan (1999) and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1989).

• Her patriotic song "Aye Mere Watan Ke Logon" (1963), written by Pradeep, moved Pandit Nehru to tears.

• Interestingly, Ustad Bismillah Khan also received the Bharat Ratna in 2001, along with Lata Mangeshkar.

NOTE

• The Bharat Ratna was instituted in 1954. The first recipients were Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, C. Rajagopalachari and Sir C. V. Raman.

• The youngest recipient is Sachin Tendulkar (2014); the first posthumous award went to Lal Bahadur Shastri (1966); the first woman recipient was Indira Gandhi (1971).

question: Nirmala Panikar received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award-2019 (given in February 2023) for her contribution to _________ dance form.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nirmala Panikar received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award-2019 (presented in February 2023) for her outstanding contribution to the "Mohiniyattam" dance form. (निर्मला पणिक्कर — मोहिनीअट्टम)

• She is a noted scholar-performer who has researched and revived traditional Mohiniyattam repertoire, and co-founded the Natanakaisiki dance school in Kerala.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mohiniyattam is the classical dance of Kerala, performed solo by women. Its name comes from "Mohini", the enchantress avatar of Lord Vishnu. It is marked by gentle, swaying (lasya) movements, off-white/gold kasavu costume, and songs in Manipravalam.

• Notable exponents: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma (called the "mother of Mohiniyattam"), Sunanda Nair, Bharati Shivaji, Kanak Rele.

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, established in 1952, is India's national academy for music, dance and drama; its highest honour is the Akademi Ratna (Fellowship).

NOTE

• Classical dances and their states: Bharatanatyam – Tamil Nadu; Kathak – Uttar Pradesh; Kathakali & Mohiniyattam – Kerala; Kuchipudi – Andhra Pradesh; Odissi – Odisha; Manipuri – Manipur; Sattriya – Assam.

question: In which city is the Rajghat memorial situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Raj Ghat" memorial is situated in Delhi, on the western bank of the river Yamuna. It marks the cremation site of Mahatma Gandhi, who was assassinated on 30 January 1948. (राजघाट — दिल्ली)

• The memorial is a simple black marble platform bearing Gandhiji's last words "Hey Ram", with an eternal flame burning at one end.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other memorials ("Ghats") along the Yamuna in Delhi:

◦ Shanti Van — Jawaharlal Nehru

◦ Shakti Sthal — Indira Gandhi

◦ Vir Bhumi — Rajiv Gandhi

◦ Vijay Ghat — Lal Bahadur Shastri

◦ Kisan Ghat — Chaudhary Charan Singh

◦ Samta Sthal — Jagjivan Ram

• Sabarmati Ashram (Ahmedabad) and Sevagram Ashram (Wardha, Maharashtra) were Gandhiji's principal ashrams.

NOTE

• Mahatma Gandhi's birthday, 2 October, is observed as Gandhi Jayanti in India and as the International Day of Non-Violence by the United Nations.

• Gandhiji is called the "Father of the Nation"; the title "Mahatma" was given by Rabindranath Tagore.

question: In the 1939 Tripuri Congress Presidential Election, Pattabhi Sitaramayya was defeated by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhas Chandra Bose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the 1939 Tripuri session of the Indian National Congress, Subhas Chandra Bose defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya, the candidate backed by Mahatma Gandhi, in the presidential election by 1580 votes to 1377. (त्रिपुरी अधिवेशन 1939 — सुभाष चंद्र बोस की जीत)

• Gandhiji described the defeat as "my own defeat". Facing non-cooperation from the Congress Working Committee, Bose resigned the presidency in April 1939 and Rajendra Prasad took over.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• After resigning, Bose formed the "Forward Bloc" in 1939 within the Congress.

• Bose had earlier been elected Congress President at the Haripura session (1938).

• He later escaped from India, reached Germany and then South-East Asia, and reorganised the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) in 1943, giving the slogans "Give me blood and I will give you freedom", "Jai Hind" and "Chalo Delhi".

NOTE

• Important Congress sessions: 1885 Bombay (W. C. Bonnerjee – first session), 1907 Surat (split), 1916 Lucknow (Congress–League Pact), 1920 Nagpur (Non-Cooperation), 1929 Lahore (Purna Swaraj – Nehru), 1931 Karachi (Fundamental Rights), 1938 Haripura and 1939 Tripuri (Bose).

question: Whose autobiography is titled ‘Waiting for a Visa’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Waiting for a Visa" is the short autobiographical work of Dr. B. R. (Bhimrao) Ambedkar, written around 1935–36. In it he recounts, through personal incidents, the humiliation of untouchability he faced in India and abroad. (वेटिंग फॉर अ वीज़ा — डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर)

• The book is prescribed as a textbook in Columbia University, where Ambedkar himself had studied.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other important works of Dr. Ambedkar: "Annihilation of Caste", "The Problem of the Rupee", "Who Were the Shudras?", "The Buddha and His Dhamma", "Thoughts on Pakistan", "States and Minorities".

• He was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and India's first Law Minister. He is called the "Father of the Indian Constitution" and was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1990.

• He founded the newspapers Mooknayak (1920) and Bahishkrit Bharat, and signed the Poona Pact (1932) with Gandhiji.

NOTE

• Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia — socialist leader, author of Wheel of History. Dr. Rajendra Prasad — India's first President, author of Atmakatha and India Divided. Dr. Kamal Ranadive — a distinguished Indian cell biologist and cancer researcher.

question: In which year was the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2019.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act" was passed by Parliament in 2019 (assented to on 9 August 2019, effective from 31 October 2019). It bifurcated the state of Jammu and Kashmir into two Union Territories — Jammu & Kashmir (with a legislature) and Ladakh (without a legislature). (जम्मू-कश्मीर पुनर्गठन अधिनियम, 2019)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Alongside it, on 5 August 2019, the special status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370 was abrogated by a Presidential Order, and Article 35A ceased to operate.

• With this, the number of States became 28 and Union Territories became 9 (later 8 after the merger of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu in January 2020).

• 31 October is also observed as National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas), the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

NOTE

• Article 3 of the Constitution empowers Parliament to form new states and alter the areas, boundaries or names of existing states.

• Recent state formations: Telangana (2014, 29th state), Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand (2000).
